_what: Phase 1 per-graph acceptance gates -- ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2-ft-session-j @ depth 30
_rule: determinism, batch invariance and padding invariance are RE-MEASURED PER GRAPH and NEVER INHERITED (ADR-015). L-2-ft reads 0.000000 batch invariance on CPU and 0.000324 on CUDA; neither is evidence about this graph.

gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_determinism.what: same token ids, repeated CUDA forwards, compared against EACH OTHER (ADR-029 amended gate). NOT against a CPU reference -- that error is what the original Session L spike made, reporting cross-provider disagreement as within-provider nondeterminism.
gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_determinism.verdict_basis: 5 repeats in one session and 1 fresh session, 600 logits each at [30,256]: bit-identical, max run-to-run delta 0.000000000. Repeats compared against EACH OTHER, never against a CPU reference.

gate_2_batch_invariance_cuda.what: one batched forward vs len(docs) sequential batch-1 forwards, same token ids, same CUDA session. Real fit slate text, not synthetic.
gate_2_batch_invariance_cuda.VERDICT: FAIL as bit-identity / PASS as ranking equivalence
gate_2_batch_invariance_cuda.verdict_basis: Batch invariance is NOT bit-exact on this graph on CUDA. Every batch size 2..30 is non-identical on 12/12 slates; max |batched - sequential| is 0.001247 at the shipping batch of 30, roughly 3.8x the shipped L-2-ft's 0.000324. Batch 1 is trivially identical. This is a real FAIL of the strict property and must not be described as invariance. Its RANKING consequence is measured in gate_2b and is nil: 0 of 229 slates change top-1, R@1 identical.

gate_3_padding_invariance_cuda.what: ADR-015's test: the SAME token ids, zero-padded to a longer tensor, nothing else changed. int8 moved a median 0.0109 and flipped top-1 in 15% of cases; the f32 graphs read 0.000000. This graph is f32 and is measured, not assumed.
gate_3_padding_invariance_cuda.verdict_basis: Bit-identical token ids zero-padded from 256 to 288/320/384/512, 40 slates x 30 pairs at each length (4,800 pairs): max |diff| 0.000000000, exactly zero on 100% of pairs, 0 top-1 flips, 0 slates reordered. ADR-015's int8 failure (median 0.0109, 15% top-1 flips) does not reproduce on this f32 graph.

gate_4_cross_provider_ranking_equivalenc.what: ADR-029's gate is RANKING equivalence, not logit identity. Both are reported.
gate_4_cross_provider_ranking_equivalenc.VERDICT: FAIL as literally worded in ADR-029 (top-10 ORDER identical on every slate) / PASS on every retrieval-visible consequence
gate_4_cross_provider_ranking_equivalenc.verdict_basis: 7 of 229 slates reorder somewhere in their top-10 and 10 of 229 anywhere in the 30. ADR-029 records 0 of 229 for the shipped L-2-ft at depth 10, so this is a real difference and it is not summarised away. What does NOT move: 0 slates change top-1, and R@1 (0.7729), R@1_current (0.7118) and R@5 (0.9520) are identical on both providers to 4 dp. session_l_gpu_recovery's own verdict text for exactly this outcome is 'RANKING REORDERS but R@1 is unchanged ... needs the human's read'.
gate_4_cross_provider_ranking_equivalenc.confound_named: This gate varies TWO things at once, because it compares the two SHIPPED paths: CUDA batched-30 against CPU sequential batch-1 (ADR-029: batching is a property of the hardware). Gate 2b isolates batching within CUDA and produces 3 top-10 reorders on its own. The two slate SETS were not intersected -- per-slate ids were not persisted -- so 'batching accounts for 3 of the 7' is NOT asserted.

comparison_L2_ft_ADR029.note: L-2-ft at depth 10, end-to-end Rust. Contrast only, NOT inherited.

gate_5_latency.what: depth 30. GPU budget is 300 ms P95 total retrieval; non-rerank stages ~6.6 ms on the GPU path. The CPU number is a CAPABILITY statement -- 1 vCPU is the fallback floor.
gate_5_latency.VERDICT: PASS on the GPU budget / CAPABILITY STATEMENT on CPU, with one consequence named
gate_5_latency.verdict_basis: CUDA batched depth 30: p50 34.53 ms, p95 40.55 ms, max 44.04 ms (tokenize+forward; forward alone p50 21.03 / p95 24.57). With ~6.6 ms of non-rerank stages that is ~47 ms P95 total against a 300 ms budget -- 16% of it. It also independently reproduces Session M's published 37.1 ms p50 (34.53 here, same order, different process). CPU sequential 1 thread depth 30: p50 1593.2 ms, p95 1777.0 ms per query, 53.1 ms per pair.
gate_5_latency.cpu_consequence_named: The CPU fallback number is reported as capability, not as a retrieval budget breach -- but it does have one downstream consequence worth stating rather than leaving implicit. ADR-029 records the CPU fallback at 199.6 ms total p50 (rerank 195.6 ms at depth 10) and calls that 27% of brief §9's 800 ms voice-to-voice budget. At depth 30 with L-6 the rerank stage alone measures 1593 ms p50, which is roughly TWICE the entire §9 budget. On a GPU machine this is irrelevant; on a CPU-only machine, depth 30 + L-6 makes voice-mode retrieval non-viable where depth 10 + L-2 was merely expensive. That is a product decision (Phase 3b's adaptive depth is the named lever), not a Phase 1 gate failure. It is also ~8.1x the shipped CPU rerank, which is more than the 3x from depth alone -- L-6 is ~2.7x L-2's per-pair CPU cost at 53.1 ms/pair.
gate_5_latency.measured_vs_plan_estimate: PLAN-R1 estimates the CPU fallback at ~1.1 s. Measured 1.59 s p50 on this machine, 45% higher. The plan's figure is an estimate and is scored as one.

_scope_limit: Every number here is measured through tools/session_i_rerankers.py -- the one verified loader -- which pins the same ORT settings the Rust stage uses (ORT_ENABLE_BASIC == Level1, 1 intra/inter-op thread, ORT_SEQUENTIAL) and the same digest-pinned tokenizer at seq 256. It is NOT a measurement of the shipped Rust rerank stage, which cannot load this graph until rerank.rs is re-pinned. No Rust was modified and nothing was shipped.

gate_2b_batching_ranking_impact_cuda._what: gate 2b -- CUDA batched(30) vs CUDA sequential(batch 1), full fit split, depth 30
gate_2b_batching_ranking_impact_cuda.VERDICT: PASS -- batching alone changes no top-1 and no R@1
gate_2b_batching_ranking_impact_cuda.verdict_basis: Provider held fixed at CUDA, only batching varies (batched 30 vs sequential 1) over the full 229-slate fit split at depth 30. 3 slates reorder within top-10, 7 anywhere in the 30, 0 change top-1, R@1 and R@1_current identical to 4 dp.

gate_6_node_placement._what: gate 6 -- node placement, L-6-ft, CUDA, batch 30 x seq 256
gate_6_node_placement._how:
Gate 6 -- node placement for L-6-ft on CUDA, using session_l_gpu_recovery's own mechanism.

`tools/session_l_gpu_recovery.py` has NO --model flag: `SHIPPED` is a module constant and its
`main()` scores the HELD-OUT slates, which would spend a held-out read as a side effect. So the
file is not modified and its main() is not run. Instead its `build()` and `placement_by_op()` --
gate 3, the node-placement mechanism ADR-029 names -- are imported and the module constant is
redirected at L-6-ft in this process only. Profiles go to scratch, not into runs/session-l.
gate_6_node_placement.VERDICT: MEASURED -- PASS on the substance (no matmul on the fallback)
gate_6_node_placement.verdict_basis: 384 of 3,264 nodes on CPUExecutionProvider = 11.76%, against 13.6% for L-2-ft in ADR-029. The fallback census is Gather 128, Unsqueeze 120, Concat 112, Reshape 8, Equal 8, Where 8 -- all shape and index ops, no matmuls, the same benign family ADR-029 documents. The hazard ADR-029 names ('a model swap could move matmuls onto the fallback') did NOT occur.
gate_6_node_placement.tool_limitation_stated_plainly: tools/session_l_gpu_recovery.py CANNOT be pointed at a model: SHIPPED is a module constant with no CLI flag, and its main() scores runs/session-m0c/slates-heldout.json -- running it as-is would spend a HELD-OUT read as a side effect, which PLAN-R1 budgets for a human decision. The file was NOT modified. Its gate-3 mechanism -- build() and placement_by_op() -- was imported and the module constant redirected in-process to L-6-ft, at the proposed batch 30 rather than the tool's RERANK_BUDGET of 10, on fit-split slates. Its gate 1 (determinism) and gate 2 (cross-provider ranking) were measured directly instead, at depth 30 on the fit split -- gates 1 and 4 above. The tool's own 4-config provider-option determinism sweep was NOT run: it exists to RECOVER determinism when provider defaults fail, and provider defaults did not fail here.

not_measured.repro_runs_2_byte_identical: NOT-MEASURED. `marlowe_eval.cli repro --runs 2` drives the release binary, which loads the digest pinned in rerank.rs. Measuring it for L-6-ft requires re-pinning Rust, which this task forbids. It remains a required Phase 1 gate and is unmet, not passed.
not_measured.held_out_R@1_delta: NOT-MEASURED, DELIBERATELY. PLAN-R1's Phase 1 kill criterion is a held-out delta <= 0, and RESULT.md records that spending a held-out read is the human's call. No held-out pool was scored with this graph in this session. Everything above is fit-split or synthetic.
not_measured.end_to_end_rust_stage: NOT-MEASURED. All numbers are the Python loader on the pinned graph. A test on a loader is not a test on the deployed stage -- the same distinction that let persona_emission.rs pass against a stale daemon.

adr_029_text_amendment_required_if_shipp: ADR-029's decision text pins 'ONE batched [10, 256] forward'. Depth 30 makes the shipped GPU tensor [30, 256]. That is an amendment to the ADR's stated shape, not a re-measurement of it, and it needs a DECISIONS.md entry rather than a silent constant change.

DISQUALIFYING.question: Does anything measured here disqualify L-6-ft at depth 30 from shipping?
DISQUALIFYING.answer: NO -- nothing measured here disqualifies it. Three things must travel with that answer.
nothing_disqualifying_because: GPU->GPU determinism is bit-identical, which is ADR-029's amended bar.
Padding invariance is exactly 0.000000 with no top-1 flips -- ADR-015's failure does not reproduce on this f32 graph.
Both providers return R@1 0.7729, R@1_current 0.7118 and R@5 0.9520, with 0 top-1 changes on 229 slates. The two paths retrieve the same thing.
37 ms of a 300 ms GPU budget, node placement 11.76% CPU with no matmuls on the fallback.
but_carry_these: Batch invariance is NOT bit-exact (max 0.001247 at batch 30, ~3.8x L-2-ft's 0.000324) and cross-provider top-10 ORDER is not identical (7 of 229 slates), where L-2-ft read 0 of 229. Under ADR-029's amended acceptance neither blocks, because the gate is ranking equivalence and top-1 does not move. Under its LITERAL wording ('top-10 order vs CPU'), gate 4 fails, and that is the human's read to make, not this session's.
Two required Phase 1 gates are NOT-MEASURED and therefore NOT PASSED: repro --runs 2 byte-identity (needs a Rust re-pin) and the held-out read (needs the human's authorisation).
The CPU fallback at depth 30 costs 1.59 s p50 per query -- ~2x brief §9's entire 800 ms voice-to-voice budget, against ADR-029's 27% for the shipped depth-10 CPU path.
